raw_case_text: A 34 year-old Thai man from Prajin Buri, a province in rural East Thailand, presented with a 4-month history of low-grade fever and multiple discrete painful umbilicated erythematous papules on his face, as well as a 40 kg weight loss from his previous normal weight of 110 kg and height of 170 cm. Two weeks prior to admission (PTA), he developed odynophagia, painful nodular ulcers on his tongue, and hoarseness of his voice. One week PTA, he had dyspnea on exertion. His medical history was unremarkable, and he denied using any pills, herbs, or intravenous drugs. His occupation was that of a car mechanic. He mentioned that he had not traveled to other locations in the previous three months. Physical examination revealed blood pressure of 90/50 mmHg, regular heart rate of 110/min, respiratory rate of 24/min, and body temperature of 38.3 C, mildly pale conjunctivae, multiple papules with central necrosis on his face painful nodular ulcers on his tongue and palate, diffuse fine crackles in both lungs, jugular vein engorgement, a positive left ventricular heave and a grade III/VI diastolic rumbling murmur at mitral valve area, hepatosplenomegaly, and mild pedal edema. The complete blood count (CBC) analysis showed a Hb of 11.1 g/dL, white blood cell of 5,350 x 103/muL, and platelets of 140,000/muL. Blood chemistries showed urea nitrogen of 56 mg/dL, creatinine of 1.98 mg/dL, total bilirubin of 4.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin of 3.09 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase of 42 U/L, alanine aminotransferase of 25 U/L, alkaline phosphatase of 147 U/L, albumin of 3.1 g/dL, corrected calcium of 13.4 mg/dL, phosphorus of 3.1 mg/dL, intact parathyroid hormone of <1.2 (normal: 15-65) pmol/L, and 1,25-OH2 vitamin D of 152 (normal: 19.9-79.3) pg/mL. Anti-HIV serology testing showed negative results. Cardiomegaly with pulmonary congestion was seen on chest radiography. Transthoracic echocardiography indicated a left ventricular ejection fraction of 54%, moderate aortic regurgitation, severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, and multiple oscillating masses on the anterior mitral valve leaflet ranging from 1.5 cm to 2.4 cm in diameter (Figure 1(a), yellow arrows). Skin scraping of the facial lesion exhibited both extracellular and intracellular yeast-like organisms with buddings, 2-4 mum in size, on Wright's stain, most likely Histoplasma. As a result, disseminated histoplasmosis and endocarditis were diagnosed, and 3 mg/kg/day intravenous liposomal amphotericin B was administered immediately. The patient had a profound cardiogenic shock and atrial fibrillation one day after being admitted to the hospital, and echocardiography indicated a mechanical obstruction of the mitral valve orifice caused by the vegetation. Three large vegetations on the anterior mitral valve leaflet were identified during emergency open-heart surgery (Figure 1(b)), and a mechanical prosthetic mitral valve was placed. Histopathology examination of the vegetation showed many yeast-like organisms. However, the patient's condition deteriorated, and he died four days after the operation from intractable multiorgan failure. The sputum and vegetation cultures grew H. capsulatum (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)) after 1 week of incubation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old Thai man presented with a 4-month history of low-grade fever, painful umbilicated facial papules, and a 40-kg weight loss, followed by 2 weeks of odynophagia, painful lingual ulcers, and hoarseness, and 1 week of exertional dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, a car mechanic from rural Prachin Buri, East Thailand, developed 4 months of low-grade fever, painful umbilicated erythematous facial papules, and 40-kg weight loss (from 110 kg to 70 kg), complicated 2 weeks prior to admission by odynophagia, painful nodular tongue ulcers, and hoarseness, and 1 week prior to admission by exertional shortness of breath.
subjective.past_medical_history: Unremarkable past medical history (undx rheumatic mitral stenosis found on echo). Social/occupational history: Car mechanic from rural Prachin Buri, East Thailand; denied pills, herbal remedies, IV drug use, or recent travel.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for low-grade fever, 40-kg weight loss, painful facial papules, painful tongue/palate ulcers, odynophagia, hoarseness, and exertional dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs: BP 90/50 mmHg, HR 110/min (regular), RR 24/min, temperature 38.3 C, height 170 cm. HEENT & skin: mildly pale conjunctivae, multiple facial papules with central necrosis, and painful nodular ulcers on the tongue and palate. Cardiovascular: jugular venous engorgement, left ventricular heave, and grade III/VI diastolic rumbling murmur at the mitral area. Respiratory: diffuse bilateral fine crackles. Abdomen & extremities: hepatosplenomegaly and mild pedal edema.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC: Hb 11.1 g/dL, WBC 5,350/uL, platelets 140,000/uL. Chemistry & endocrine: BUN 56 mg/dL, creatinine 1.98 mg/dL, total bilirubin 4.9 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 3.09 mg/dL, AST 42 U/L, ALT 25 U/L, ALP 147 U/L, albumin 3.1 g/dL, corrected calcium 13.4 mg/dL, phosphorus 3.1 mg/dL, intact PTH <1.2 pmol/L (normal 15-65), 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D 152 pg/mL (normal 19.9-79.3); anti-HIV serology negative. Chest X-ray: cardiomegaly with pulmonary congestion. TTE: LVEF 54%, moderate aortic regurgitation, severe rheumatic mitral stenosis, and multiple large oscillating vegetations (1.5-2.4 cm) on the anterior mitral valve leaflet causing mechanical mitral orifice obstruction on hospital day 2.
objective.advanced_workup: Wright-stained skin scraping of facial papule: intracellular and extracellular 2-4 um budding yeast-like organisms. Emergency open-heart mitral valve replacement pathology & microbiology: 3 large anterior mitral leaflet vegetations showing abundant yeast-like organisms on histopathology; sputum and mitral valve vegetation fungal cultures grew Histoplasma capsulatum after 1 week.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Disseminated histoplasmosis complicated by native-valve Histoplasma capsulatum mitral endocarditis (on severe rheumatic mitral stenosis) and 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D-mediated hypercalcemia in an HIV-negative patient. Confirmation: Facial lesion Wright stain and excised mitral valve vegetation histopathology showing 2-4 um budding yeasts, and positive sputum and mitral vegetation cultures isolating Histoplasma capsulatum. Plan & clinical course: Initiated immediately on IV liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day) and underwent emergency mechanical mitral valve replacement on hospital day 2 for obstructive mitral vegetations, cardiogenic shock, and atrial fibrillation, but died 4 days postoperatively from intractable multiorgan failure.
